correctness.rationale: The frozen homotopy formula is mathematically correct, but needs the prior-coverage correction explained below. For its Morse proof, the only extensions in row zero of a given nonempty outside-row face come from centers in rows 0, 1, 3. A row-two singleton can extend only by the row-zero vertex in its own column; a row-one or row-three singleton in column c can extend by the two row-zero vertices at c±1 from T_(0,c); for larger faces the same column restrictions either allow only one row-zero vertex or place both possible vertices in a single T_(0,c). The nonextendible residual faces are exactly the horizontal row-two distance-two edges, the four triangles of each row-two-centered tetrahedron and those tetrahedra. The new one-dimensional gradient move loses a row-two vertex on any non-backtracking descent and cannot return to a new lower edge. The new two-dimensional move ends on a first-dimensional paired upper face or a critical triangle, with no further upward move. Together with the acyclic fiber matchings this leaves one loop and n two-cells per parity; the integral column-step cocycle evaluates to n on each row-zero cycle even at n=6, so no attaching degree to either loop is nonzero. The full face vector follows since pairs at distance two have at most two common neighbors and each vertex of the neighborhood complex has seven neighbors. Verification notes and expected finite output were inspected; the universal proof does not depend on running them. The repaired proof has been checked independently. In each parity, a maximal neighborhood tetrahedron has a middle-column rung and flank endpoints at c±1 in one row. Even at n=6 the endpoints have exactly one common graph neighbor; the displayed triangle-tetrahedron and then edge-triangle deletions are elementary and leave exactly the four triangular faces on each slab of consecutive rungs. There are two collapses per original tetrahedron, 8n in total. In any tetrahedron transfer t times the smaller flank weight out of both flanks and into both rung vertices. The sums and nonnegativity are preserved; on overlaps the minimum vanishes, and the formula is invariant under the allowed rung and flank permutations. It therefore gives the claimed strong coordinate-equivariant deformation. The sphere union has a CW skeleton of n rungs plus n joining edges, a connected graph of cycle rank one. One two-cell per sphere attaches in its own three-edge arc, so all are nullhomotopic. For the new disk assertion the full group is transitive on spheres of both parities. A point with support in two columns lies in a unique sphere. Points supported in one column have no orbit identifications within a given sphere beyond those from row swaps and column exchange in its stabilizer. The local permutation group consists of the independent pair swaps and the block exchange, and both act as asserted. Radial projection identifies the independent-swap quotient with the sector X,Y≥0 of the unit sphere. Coordinates B=(X−Y)/sqrt(2) and Z identify this sector with 2B²+Z²≤1; the remaining block swap is central inversion there and gives a closed disk by the radius-preserving angle-doubling map. Thus the full ordinary orbit space retracts to a disk, not merely a rationally acyclic space. These arguments verify the revised RESULT.md, SLOGAN.txt and scientific verification notes under /workspace/repairs/2/. No equivariance of the individual simplicial collapse ordering or of a wedge decomposition is claimed.

The same-day three-cut record calculates S(G)≃S¹∨n S² by capping the meridians in a torus. Its S(G) is an additional close homotopy model: for a bipartite graph with at most two common neighbors per pair, adjoining the cone on each neighborhood simplex on one shore, based at its opposite-shore center, gives a common expansion. Faces of size ≥3 on the first shore have a unique center and can be removed in decreasing dimension against their coned cofaces; for pairs with one center remove the pair against its remaining triangle. Pairs with two centers leave the two triangles triangulating a square, recovering the square filling. The other collapse deletes the cones to return the neighborhood component.

value.rationale: In the first shorter period excluded from the PL torus theorem, the intrinsic geometry is not merely a Betti-number list: each component retains a cycle of spheres glued along specified edges, while the full coordinate-dihedral quotient has a disk as an explicit geometric spine. This distinguishes the effect of the short C4 factor from the sphere quotient of cycle-square neighborhood tori and permits work with actual symmetries and fixed subsets rather than only an abstract ordinary wedge. The value of the repaired quotient and embedded model does not rest on reasserting the previously covered circulant special cases or presenting already-used move formulas as new.
